Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. fulfillment: The node’s binding is too broad and its traces appear to judge the requested relation from the edited image alone. In the source, there is one blue mug left of the headphones; in the edited image, the headphones are altered and there are two visible mugs, one on each side. The right-hand mug may satisfy the final positional relation, but that alone does not establish that the original mug was moved there or that the requested edit is complete; the left-hand mug and blurred blue region also make object identity and edit continuity ambiguous. Tighten the binding to the original mug and headphones, and make the criterion assess progress from source to edited image as well as the final relation: distinguish a completed move from partial progress such as duplication or an unresolved identity match. Do not force “partial” from the reference label; require image-grounded evidence for the classification, and use unknown if identity or change cannot be resolved. The two support observations are highly confident but not independent (s2 depends on s1), so avoid treating their agreement as corroboration. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a semantic evidence/binding and criterion issue.
s2: The binding and criterion should compare the source and edited images, not merely ask whether any visible mug is right of the headphones. Bind the target to the original blue mug using observable appearance and location, then assess whether that same object’s requested relocation is evidenced; explicitly distinguish a final right-side relation from duplication or an unresolved identity match. Here the edited image shows two mugs, headphones that differ from the source, and a blurred blue region where the original mug was, so the right-hand mug alone does not establish completion, while the left mug/blur may indicate progress but leave continuity uncertain. Require evidence for both identity/change and final relation, and preserve unknown when those cannot be resolved rather than inferring a label from the reference. Treat the dependent, high-confidence support traces as one observation, not corroboration. This is a semantic binding/evidence issue; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported.
s1: The current binding is truncated/ambiguous and checks only whether some mug and headphones can be compared in the edited image. Make this support node explicitly compare source and edited images, binding the target to the original blue mug and the headphones by their observable appearance and location. Its criterion should report evidence availability for identity, change, and relative placement—not infer fulfillment merely because a mug is now to the headphones’ right. The source has one blue mug left of the headphones; the edit shows a blurred blue region at the former mug location, two smaller mugs on opposite sides, and visibly altered headphones. These observations make continuity and the extent of progress uncertain, so preserve unknown where identity/change cannot be resolved and avoid treating the right-hand mug alone as proof that the original mug was moved. Keep this node’s support role distinct from the downstream yes/no/partial fulfillment judgment; the reference label constrains the aggregate but is not atomic ground truth. High confidence in the existing trace does not resolve the binding problem, and dependent traces are not independent corroboration. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; address semantic binding and evidence criteria.
